original_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero and fix an integer g >= 0. Does there exist a positive constant b(X,g) such that every reduced irreducible curve C subset X whose normalization has genus g satisfies C^2 >= -b(X,g)?
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Conjecture 3.3.4, "Weak bounded negativity." This is the paper's genus-fixed bounded-negativity question for reduced, irreducible curves on a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the core content of Conjecture 3.3.4: the ambient object is a smooth projective surface X in characteristic zero; the desired bound is a positive constant depending only on X and the fixed genus; the curves are reduced and irreducible; and your phrase "whose normalization has genus g" matches the paper's definition of geometric genus. It also correctly does not impose smoothness on C, which is important because the smooth-curve variant is a different conjecture, namely Conjecture 3.3.5. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states g > 0, not g >= 0. Allowing g = 0 broadens the question beyond the official formulation of Conjecture 3.3.4. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
The paper uses the strict inequality C^2 > -b(X,g), not the non-strict inequality C^2 >= -b(X,g). ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, the quantifiers should be explicit: for each smooth projective surface X in characteristic zero and each fixed positive integer g, there exists a positive constant b(X,g) such that the bound holds for every reduced, irreducible curve C ⊂ X of geometric genus g. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The paper phrases the condition as "C has geometric genus g," and immediately defines this as "the genus of the normalization of C." That definition should be stated explicitly in the final version. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

It is useful to say explicitly that C^2 denotes the self-intersection number of C on X; the paper treats this as standard and leaves it implicit in the conjecture's wording. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero, and let g > 0 be a fixed integer. Does there exist a positive constant b(X,g) such that every reduced, irreducible curve C ⊂ X of geometric genus g (equivalently, such that the normalization of C has genus g) satisfies the self-intersection bound C^2 > -b(X,g)? ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's Conjecture 3.3.4, not the broader Bounded Negativity Conjecture 3.3.1 and not the smooth-curve variant Conjecture 3.3.5. The decisive features are exactly the ones in your draft: a bound depending on X and a fixed genus g, applied to reduced, irreducible curves, with genus understood as geometric genus via normalization. Example 3.3.3 gives the motivating positive-characteristic obstruction: on X = C x C in characteristic p > 0, there are smooth curves of fixed genus whose self-intersection tends to minus infinity, which explains why the conjecture is stated in characteristic zero and with fixed genus. The nearby partial result in Section 3.5 confirms this reading: Proposition 3.5.3 proves that if kappa(X) > 0, then every reduced, irreducible curve C of geometric genus g(C) on X satisfies C^2 > c1(X)^2 - 3c2(X) + 2 - 2g(C), i.e. an explicit genus-dependent lower bound of exactly the same type. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
